$comment: GENHUB - launch checklist. ONE source of truth: scripts/setup-env.mjs reads this file, and so does the admin Setup tab (src/lib/setup-check.ts). Keeping it in one place is deliberate - when these lived apart the terminal and the website could tell you different things. Order is cheapest-first: free work before anything that needs a card. `sensitive: true` means the value must never be echoed back to a browser; the API reports only its shape.
$rulesComment: The classification rules live here too, as regex sources, for the same reason the checklist does. These were originally written twice - once in the script and once in the app - and the two disagreed on the very first real value they saw: .env.local held BUNNY_TOKEN_SECRET="dev-token-secret-...", the app called it configured and the script called it a placeholder. Two renderers, two answers, about one file. Now both compile these strings. `placeholder` must NOT match 'default' or a bare 'xxx': Upstash issues rediss://default:<password>@... and real hostnames contain xxx.

groups.title: Legal identity
groups.blurb: 18 U.S.C. 2257 requires a named records custodian at a real place of business. It does NOT require a company: an individual is allowed. Selling adult content without this is criminal exposure, not a missing feature.

items.title: Records custodian name
items.site: Your ID, or your BRELA certificate
steps: No company required: 28 C.F.R. 75.2 allows an individual to be the custodian
Easiest path with nothing to register: your own full legal name as it appears on your national ID or passport
If you already have a registered entity, use that instead - most commonly the name on your HarakaPay merchant account, which is a real registered business you already trade through
Use your BRELA certificate only if you have one; do not wait for one to launch

items.title: Place of business
items.site: Anywhere real - read the trade-off first
steps: A real street address where the records could actually be inspected. A P.O. Box alone does not satisfy the requirement
This address is PUBLISHED on /2257 and is public. That is the only real cost of the individual path

Your home address is legally sufficient. If you would rather not publish it, a serviced business-centre or virtual-office address works, provided someone there can actually produce the records on request
Registering a company only to obtain an address is the slowest and most expensive of the three options
items.example: NEXT_PUBLIC_COMPANY_ADDRESS=Plot 42, Nyerere Road, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania

items.title: Compliance inbox
steps: An address that DMCA notices, takedown requests and compliance mail can reach
A personal Gmail is acceptable; a role address on your domain looks more credible

groups.title: Database
groups.blurb: Nothing exists without this. Right now DATABASE_URL points at your laptop, so a deploy would start completely empty.

items.title: Managed Postgres
steps: Sign up (GitHub is fastest)
Create project -> Name: genhub -> Region: closest to Tanzania
On the connection string panel, turn ON the 'Pooled connection' toggle
Copy the string starting postgresql://
Then run: npm run db:deploy
items.mustHint: This is the DIRECT connection. A serverless app opens a connection per instance and will exhaust the direct limit under load - use the pooled host.

groups.title: Rate limiting
groups.blurb: Without this, rate limits are per-instance and reset on every deploy, so the login limiter stops holding under load.

anyOf.mustHint: The Upstash REST endpoint is always https:// - check you copied the REST URL and not the TCP one.
plaintext redis:// sends your data unencrypted. Managed Redis should always be rediss:// (TLS).

items.title: Managed Redis
steps: Sign up
Create Database -> Type: Regional -> TLS: enabled
Open the 'Connect' tab - Upstash offers TWO pairs and either works

Recommended: the REST pair, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL + UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN (two lines). It is an HTTPS connection, so it suits serverless deploys and cannot leave a TCP pool open between invocations
Alternative: choose Node / ioredis and copy the single URL starting rediss:// (two s characters) into REDIS_URL

groups.title: Transactional email
groups.blurb: Without this a user who forgets their password is locked out permanently - reset emails only reach the server log.

items.title: API key
steps: Create account
Domains -> Add Domain -> enter your domain
Add the DNS records (SPF/DKIM) at your registrar, wait for status 'Verified'
API Keys -> Create API Key (permission: Sending access)
Copy the key starting re_ - you see it ONCE and never again

items.title: Sender address
steps: Must be on the domain you verified, otherwise every email lands in spam

groups.title: Video hosting
groups.blurb: The single most important account: without it creators cannot upload anything and no video can stream. The catalogue would be empty.

items.title: Stream library ID
steps: Sign up, verify your email
Left menu: Stream -> Add Library -> Name: genhub
Open the library -> tab 'API'
Copy 'Library ID' (a number)

items.title: Stream API key
steps: Library -> tab 'API' -> copy 'API Key'

items.title: CDN hostname
steps: Library -> tab 'API' -> copy 'CDN Hostname' WITHOUT the https:// part
items.forbidHint: Store the bare hostname. The app adds the scheme itself.

items.title: Token authentication key
steps: Library -> tab 'Security'
Turn ON 'Token Authentication' <- REQUIRED, otherwise anyone with a copied link watches paid video for free
Copy the 'Token Authentication Key'

items.title: Allow your own domain to play video
steps: Pull Zone -> Security -> Allowed Referrers (referrer / hotlink protection)
Add your live domain, e.g. https://genhub.co.tz
Add http://localhost:3000 as well, or video cannot be tested locally
Any host NOT on this list gets a 403 for the manifest and for every segment, so the player only spins

items.title: Storage zone
steps: Menu: Storage -> Add Storage Zone -> Name: genhub-thumbs

items.title: Storage password
steps: Storage zone -> tab 'FTP & API Access' -> on 'Password' click Copy/Show

groups.title: Money
groups.blurb: This is the one that made your own payments fail. HarakaPay accepts the request and reports "USSD push sent", but with a zero float the prompt never settles and the order stays processing forever. It is a balance on their side, not a variable in a file - and on some accounts there is no button that credits it, so their support has to.

items.title: Fund the merchant float
steps: Sign in to https://harakapay.net/dashboard and finish any "start receiving payments" / activation prompt - live collections will not settle until the account itself is activated

Look for a top-up on the Wallet/Float card. Many accounts have none: Float and Wallet (94%) are balances that HarakaPay credits, so if there is nothing to click, ask their support in writing how the float is funded on your account
Ask them which balance a deposit lands in, and send your order ids (and the order where the customer approved but nothing settled) as the evidence
It is funded when GET /api/v1/balance reports float_balance above 0 - the app refuses USSD collects until then
Prove it from your own phone: npm run smoke:harakapay:live

groups.title: Go live
groups.blurb: HarakaPay cannot reach a localhost webhook, so until this is done settlements rely on polling. Everything else can be tested before you get here.

items.title: Public URL
steps: Buy a domain (Cloudflare / Namecheap / Truehost)
Enter https://yourdomain.com with NO trailing slash
Vercel -> Add New -> Project -> Import Git Repository
Environment Variables -> add every variable from .env.local
Deploy -> Settings -> Domains -> add your domain (TLS is automatic)
items.mustHint: Must be the real public https:// URL - it is baked into SEO tags, webhook callbacks and referral links.
